1.why: All five screens are static single-card pages with no animations, moving images, or pop-ups.

2.why: Bold headings, bold field labels, and solid high-contrast primary buttons stand out, although the dark logs panel visually competes with them for attention.

3.why: Each page presents one focused task with a single primary action so Helena can find what to do quickly, though the six-digit code she needs sits in the logs block at the bottom of the page.

4.why: Every screen states its own instruction and the password policy is displayed inline, so little must be memorized beyond copying the two codes shown on screen.

5.why: No 'remember me', autofill, or password-manager option appears on any screen; the only convenience offered is permission to paste the recovery code manually.

6.why: The email field starts empty and no saved account identifier is shown, and the only pre-filled value is a long random recovery token the user would not recognize as familiar.

7.why: Body text is short and plain-language (e.g., 'Enter the email address registered for your healthcare account'), with only occasional formal phrasing such as the privacy-note sentence.

8.why: Only the happy path is shown across the five screenshots, so no error message demonstrating problem-plus-fix guidance is present in the system as observed.

9.why: No illustrative examples such as a sample email or example password are given, although the pre-filled recovery token and the visible code 246810 do show what to type.

10.why: The flow offers no choice between authentication methods (password, code, or face login); it is a single fixed path, so no such choices exist to be clear.

11.why: Each screen shows at most two input fields and two buttons, never presenting too many choices at one time.

12.why: Each action produces a visible outcome ('Accepted securely. Hospital appointment booking may proceed.', log lines like 'password reset completed'), though some confirmations are in technical log wording.

13.why: Every new step includes a one-line tip ('Use at least 14 characters...', 'Review the statement before confirming.') plus the recurring 'Stay safe' note.

14.why: The 'Start over' button on the verification screen and the editable forms let the user try again, although no in-error retry path is demonstrated.

15.why: All steps share the same header, card layout, button styling, and 'Stay safe' footer, so the design stays consistent and learnable over time.
